In September 1995, she was admitted for investigation. When reviewed in January 1996, the spasms had ceased and there was almost complete resolution of the axial stiffness and the hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine. When reviewed four months later, she was receiving vigabatrin 2 g/d, slow-release carbamazepine 600 mg/d, and clonazepam 2.5 mg/d.
Further questioning at this time revealed that a mild degree of back stiffness had been present for three to four years prior to the recent deterioration.

Despite discontinuing the lamotrigine, the symptoms persisted. In retrospect, the symptoms of SMS had probably been present to a mild degree for three to four years, and the vigabatrin had been suppressing the symptoms of SMS, which only became significant following the withdrawal of the drug.

On admission she was receiving only carbamazepine. Examination showed a marked hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine and rigidity of the abdominal muscles. Tone was increased in the legs, and the tendon reflexes were brisk in the arms and legs. The abdominal reflexes were preserved, the right plantar response was flexor and the left extensor. Sensory examination was normal. EMG showed continuous motor unit activity in the axial musculature, and exteroceptive reflexes, elicited from the posterior tibial nerve at the ankle, were abnormally pronounced. Two months later, she noticed increasing back stiffness and occasional spasms affecting the trunk and legs without any stimulus sensitivity.
